records.issue_text: [BUG] The dataclass default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition (module import) time, so every AssignmentSource constructed via `from_integration` gets the worker-process start time instead of the actual queue time. The `queued` field is always stale by however long the process has been running — on a long-lived celery worker it can be hours/days off — and any future staleness-based logic (e.g. dropping stale assignment syncs) silently uses wrong data; it also masks that the value is fixed at import, making it impossible to reason about when an assignment actually originated.
records.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). That expression is evaluated at import/class-definition time, so all instances created without explicitly passing `queued` (including `from_integration`, which only passes `source_name` and `integration_id`) will share the same stale timestamp from when the worker process loaded the module. This is a real correctness bug; it should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The task calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...) but the abstract sync_assignee_outbound in the mixin and all concrete provider implementations were never given an assignment_source parameter — the parameter was instead added to sync_status_outbound. For every real integration (Jira, VSTS, GitHub, etc.), a synced assignee change raises TypeError: sync_assignee_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source', killing the celery task and breaking assignee sync entirely; only the mock-based tests pass, masking the breakage.

records.issue_text: [BUG] sync_group_assignee_outbound passes assignment_source.to_dict() containing a raw datetime (`queued`) as an apply_async kwarg, which the celery JSON serializer cannot encode, so the sync task fails at publish time and the assignee sync is silently dropped while the caller (GroupAssignee.objects.assign) reports success. When the JSON task serializer is in use (Sentry's hardening direction), every assign/deassign with an inbound assignment_source raises a serialization error inside the fire-and-forget apply_async; the group is still assigned locally, but the outbound sync to OTHER linked integrations never runs and no error reaches the user — the exact partial-success the cycle-prevention design is meant to preserve. The fix is to omit `queued` from to_dict (or serialize it to an ISO string), since nothing consumes it.
